newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ENGLAND ON BRINK OF VICTORY AGAINST N.Z..
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND ON BRINK OF VICTORY AGAINST N.Z..

text.p: England were poised to turn their tour of New Zealand and Zimbabwe around at lunch on Tuesday, the last day of the first cricket test at Eden Park.
New Zealand were teetering at 105 for eight wickets in their second innings, still needing to reach 131 to make England bat again and with only one specialist batsman, Nathan Astle, remaining.

Fine spin bowling by left-armer Phil Tufnell backed by a seamer Alan Mullally plus some self-destruction by the home side saw New Zealand crumble from a shaky 56 for three overnight to their precarious lunch-time position.
On this tour England have been slammed by the media for drawing a test series against lowly Zimbabwe and losing the one-day series there.
After two wins in their warm-up games the first two days of this test began in similar vein to the Zimbabwe section as New Zealand reached 390 after being sent in.
But a powerful England innings of 521 built around centuries by Alec Stewart and Graham Thorpe gave the tourists a winning chance.
After starting the morning confidently, New Zealand soon dug themselves into deeper trouble when captain Lee Germon was needlessly run out by a direct throw by Nasser Hussain.
Justin Vaughan was then trapped lbw by Tufnell from a ball which spun viciously from the rough.
Adam Parore danced down the wicket to Tufnell and was easily stumped by Stewart for 33.
Mullally then chipped in by inducing Chris Cairns to chop a ball on to his stumps and had Dipak Patel leg before for nought last ball before lunch.
Tufnell caused most problems for the New Zealand batsmen.
In the morning session, he had figures of two for six from 12 overs while Mullally had taken two for 13 in 11 tidy overs.
